This file holds the robustness analyses summarized in the article: the
convergent check against routing (Table S1, Fig. S1), the known-truth
simulation (Table S2), the two machine-learning checks (Table S3), the
cause-specific odds ratios (Table S4) and the unknown-cause diagnostic
(Table S5). All tables are generated by the analysis pipeline from its outputs.

## S1. Convergent check against routing

The friction-surface travel time from each sampled district centroid to the
nearest public complex hospital was compared with the OSRM driving time to the
three nearest hospitals by straight line (shortest of the three). The
pre-specified sample (200 centroids, stratified by travel-time quintile; 199
routed) carries the pre-specified rule, Spearman of at least 0.80 outside the
Amazon, evaluated on the five Amazon departments used as a proxy at the time.
The basin and altitude strata are post hoc. The enriched sample (150 districts
with a mean travel time above 45 minutes; 149 routed) oversamples the remote
tail on purpose and is never pooled with the pre-specified one.

**Table S1.** Agreement between friction-surface and OSRM travel times.
Bootstrap 95 % CIs over centroids; the ratio is the median of OSRM over
friction minutes for the same centroids.

| Sample and stratum | n | Spearman | CI low | CI high | Median OSRM/friction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-specified: all | 199 | 0.738 | 0.637 | 0.821 | 1.17 |
| Pre-specified: outside the five Amazon departments (pre-specified rule) | 174 | 0.801 | 0.733 | 0.854 | 1.20 |
| Pre-specified: outside the Amazon basin (post hoc) | 86 | 0.850 | 0.752 | 0.912 | 1.09 |
| Pre-specified: Amazon basin (post hoc) | 113 | 0.653 | 0.489 | 0.790 | 1.22 |
| Pre-specified: Amazon basin, <500 m (post hoc) | 17 | 0.513 | −0.057 | 0.919 | 0.82 |
| Pre-specified: Amazon basin, ≥500 m (post hoc) | 96 | 0.705 | 0.575 | 0.818 | 1.27 |
| Enriched remote sample: all | 149 | 0.400 | 0.234 | 0.553 | 1.00 |
| Enriched remote sample: outside the basin | 73 | 0.511 | 0.302 | 0.677 | 1.05 |
| Enriched remote sample: Amazon basin | 76 | 0.330 | 0.085 | 0.553 | 0.79 |

For six pairs of departmental capitals (Lima–Ica, Trujillo–Chiclayo,
Cusco–Puno, Arequipa–Moquegua, Huancayo–Ayacucho and Piura–Tumbes), the mean
absolute percentage difference between friction and OSRM times was 18.0 %,
largest for Huancayo–Ayacucho (38.1 %).

![**Fig. S1.** Friction-surface travel time against OSRM routing time for the sampled district centroids, by stratum (log scales; the dashed line is equality). Filled markers: pre-specified sample; hollow markers: enriched remote sample. Two centroids with a zero time are not drawn.](media/FigS1_osrm.pdf){width=60%}

## S2. Known-truth simulation

Deaths were aggregated into cells (district × age group × sex × cause group;
6,889 cells, 70,496 deaths) and outcomes were simulated with the observed
baseline odds, a district random intercept with standard deviation 0.551 and a
planted odds ratio per 60 minutes. Each replicate was refitted with the main
estimator. Monte Carlo standard errors (MCSE) follow Morris, White and Crowther
(2019).

**Table S2.** Operating characteristics of the RQ3 estimator. FP: false-positive
rate at a planted odds ratio of 1.00. Pre-specified limits: FP ≤ 7 %, bias
≤ 10 %, coverage 92–97 %.

| Planted OR | Replications | Mean OR | Bias (%) | Coverage (%) | Coverage MCSE | Power or FP rate (%) | FP MCSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 500 | — | — | — | — | 7.6 | 1.2 |
| 1.10 | 200 | 1.097 | −0.2 | 90.0 | 2.1 | 99.0 | — |
| 1.20 | 200 | 1.201 | 0.0 | 92.5 | 1.9 | 100.0 | — |
| 1.50 | 200 | 1.485 | −1.0 | 93.5 | 1.7 | 100.0 | — |

## S3. Machine-learning checks

Two checks were subordinate to the main analysis and validated by leaving one
department out. (a) A calibration of log(OSRM/friction) on the routed
centroids, compared with a constant ratio and with ratios by trip-length band;
the selected model enters the article only as a sensitivity variant.
(b) A gradient-boosting classifier of death outside a facility, monotone in
travel time, compared with and without travel time; the change in Brier score
(ΔBrier, positive when travel time helps) carries a district-block bootstrap CI
and a within-department permutation of travel time.

**Table S3a.** Calibration of the OSRM-to-friction ratio. MAPE: mean absolute
percentage error in minutes; remote Spearman: in districts with a mean of
45 minutes or more.

| Model | MAPE (%) | Remote Spearman | κ at 60 min | κ at 120 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Constant ratio (baseline) | 205.6 | 0.431 | 0.686 | 0.371 |
| Band ratios | 182.1 | 0.425 | 0.596 | 0.356 |
| Ridge (regularized linear) | 58.5 | 0.602 | 0.691 | 0.490 |
| Isotonic on friction time | 176.3 | 0.424 | 0.570 | 0.293 |
| Gradient boosting (monotone) | 126.4 | 0.459 | 0.556 | 0.425 |

**Table S3b.** Predictive contribution of travel time to death outside a
facility.

| Population | Deaths | ΔBrier | CI low | CI high | Permutation drop | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| All causes | 593,438 | 0.00313 | 0.00173 | 0.00479 | 0.00395 | Contribution not refuted |
| Amenable causes | 70,496 | −0.00292 | −0.00574 | −0.00012 | 0.00282 | No positive contribution |

The all-cause contribution mirrors the non-specific gradient of the all-cause
model in the article; among amenable causes travel time did not improve the
prediction.

## S6. Further checks

- **Misplaced hospitals.** Placing the two hospitals with gross coordinate
  errors at their district centroid changed the 60-minute class of 1.12 % of
  districts (pre-specified limit 5 %).
- **Districts without a polygon.** Excluding the 12 provinces that contain the
  21 census districts without a polygon left 1,759 districts; the share of
  residents beyond 60 minutes was 10.6 % (10.9 % with all districts) and beyond
  120 minutes 4.4 % (4.6 %).
- **Local clusters.** Significant local Moran clusters numbered 235 (queen
  contiguity), 266 (four neighbors) and 456 (eight neighbors), a variation of
  69 % against the pre-specified maximum of 25 %; global Moran's I was
  significant and positive under all three.
- **Registration completeness.** The correlation between district deaths per
  1,000 residents and travel time was −0.108, below the pre-specified flag of
  |r| > 0.30.
